sequences.title: Route Reception at a Route Reflector

intro.quote: When an RR receives a route from an IBGP peer, it selects the best path based on its path selection rule.

steps.explain: The IBGP peer supplies the route to the route reflector, which selects the best path.

cite.quote: When an RR receives a route from an IBGP peer, it selects the best path based on its path selection rule.

sequences.title: Reflecting a Non-Client Route to Clients

intro.quote: When an RR receives a route from an IBGP peer, it selects the best path based on its path selection rule.

steps.explain: For a route received from a non-client peer, the route reflector reflects the route to all client peers.

cite.quote: A route from a Non-Client IBGP peer: Reflect to all the Clients.

intro.quote: When an RR receives a route from an IBGP peer, it selects the best path based on its path selection rule.

steps.explain: For a route received from a client peer, the route reflector reflects the route to all non-client peers and also to the client peers.

cite.quote: A route from a Client peer: Reflect to all the Non-Client peers and also to the Client peers.

intro.quote: ORIGINATOR_ID is a new optional, non-transitive BGP attribute of Type code 9.

fields.name: ORIGINATOR_ID
fields.explain: A route reflector creates this optional, non-transitive attribute when reflecting a route, and it carries the BGP Identifier of the route originator in the local AS. A router that recognizes it should ignore a route whose ORIGINATOR_ID is its own BGP Identifier.

cite.quote: ORIGINATOR_ID is a new optional, non-transitive BGP attribute of Type code 9. This attribute is 4 bytes long and it will be created by an RR in reflecting a route. This attribute will carry the BGP Identifier of the originator of the route in the local AS. A BGP speaker SHOULD NOT create an ORIGINATOR_ID attribute if one already exists. A router that recognizes the ORIGINATOR_ID attribute SHOULD ignore a route received with its BGP Identifier as the ORIGINATOR_ID.

intro.quote: CLUSTER_LIST is a new, optional, non-transitive BGP attribute of Type code 10. It is a sequence of CLUSTER_ID values representing the reflection path that the route has passed.

fields.name: CLUSTER_LIST
fields.explain: This variable-length attribute records the route's reflection path as a sequence of cluster identifiers. A route reflector prepends its local identifier, and it should ignore an advertisement when that identifier is already in the list.

cite.quote: CLUSTER_LIST is a new, optional, non-transitive BGP attribute of Type code 10. It is a sequence of CLUSTER_ID values representing the reflection path that the route has passed. When an RR reflects a route, it MUST prepend the local CLUSTER_ID to the CLUSTER_LIST. If the CLUSTER_LIST is empty, it MUST create a new one. Using this attribute an RR can identify if the routing information has looped back to the same cluster due to misconfiguration. If the local CLUSTER_ID is found in the CLUSTER_LIST, the advertisement received SHOULD be ignored.

intro.quote: However, this represents a single point of failure so to make it possible to have multiple RRs in the same cluster, all RRs in the same cluster can be configured with a 4-byte CLUSTER_ID so that an RR can discard routes from other RRs in the same cluster.

fields.name: CLUSTER_ID
fields.explain: Within one cluster, route reflectors can use a four-byte identifier so that a route reflector can discard routes from other route reflectors in that cluster.

cite.quote: However, this represents a single point of failure so to make it possible to have multiple RRs in the same cluster, all RRs in the same cluster can be configured with a 4-byte CLUSTER_ID so that an RR can discard routes from other RRs in the same cluster.
